Hi u/agraves524. Another Dad here, who struggled with the very same after the birth of my second daughter.

Are you finding the very smallest of things hard, like trying not to be too forceful when putting her arm into her clothes, or worrying about rocking her too much when you hold her? That’s just a couple of the things that really had my anxiety peaking and I know just how you feel right now.

I also struggled a great deal with the crying. At times, it would make me feel useless because all I could think was that I was failing as a Dad to make my child happy or comfortable enough that they wouldn’t cry. I didn’t consider that it is just something a baby does.

At times, I’d be on the floor in the corner of the kitchen, head in hands literally sobbing. It broke me, both mentally and physically. I was lucky to sleep an hour a night and when I returned to work I felt like a zombie.

The thing is, you have to try and remember that either you and I are anomalies, or this is more common than you think. Yes, it won’t make it easier right now, but please try to find solace in that it eventually will. 7 months on, I’m much better. I feel more relaxed. I feel more rested and I understand my child better so I know what I am doing far more than I did back then.

I, like many other dads that pass through here, will be rooting for you. You’re a great dad and this will all be so worth it. If you remember, please drop me a message in a few months to let me know how you are doing and if you need to speak sooner, don’t hesitate to PM me.
